title: Split-flat finite filtered sheaf models and their canonical comparisons
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to a coefficient universe and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Work in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with flatness as in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], decreasing filtrations [def-sp-filtration] on cochain complexes and their step and graded quotients [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Use the bounded-above, uniformly finite filtered chain categories $\mathcal C_{[a,b],-}$, their graded quasi-isomorphisms and their formal localizations from [def-trf-uniform-finite-filtered-localization]. A filtered complex $K$ is degreewise split-flat if for each degree $n$ there are a finite family of flat sheaves $B_i$, integer grade labels $g_i$, and an isomorphism $\bigoplus_i B_i\simeq K^n$ identifying $F^pK^n$ with the sum of the images of summands with $g_i\ge p$. No compatibility of these splittings with the differential is imposed. In the fixed interval, zero summands outside it can be deleted, giving summands only in grades $a,\ldots,b$. Let the split-flat chain category be the full subcategory on these objects. A filtered chain homotopy is a usual chain homotopy each of whose components restricts from $F^pK^n$ to $F^pL^m$ for every $p,n,m$. Form the quotient category by this relation and its full subcategory of bounded-above split-flat objects in $[a,b]$. Its graded quasi-isomorphisms are homotopy classes represented by maps which are quasi-isomorphisms on every graded complex. For $[a,b]\subseteq[c,d]$, interval widening preserves the uniform filtration-bound property, leaves objects and maps unchanged, and gives inclusion functors on chain and split-flat homotopy categories; localize these inclusions by the canonical localization universal property. Use the canonical direct-sum total tensor and zero-morphism infrastructure of [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For two filtered complexes $P,W$, its tensor-step arrow is the total tensor of the inclusions $F^pP\to P$ and $F^qW\to W$. A decreasing filtration $F$ on $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes W)$ is the convolution filtration if $F^s$ is the image of the coproduct of these arrows over $p+q=s$, equivalently the sum of their images. This is a characterization of actual subobjects, not a choice of a filtration from a mere existence theorem.

source.place: §5.2.1(b), finite filtered flat-model interface for the agent-formulated resolution tool; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tags 077J and 06YQ, and derived.tex Tag 05S2. Splittings are termwise; tensor steps are the canonical total tensor of inclusions.

proof.text: For widenProperty, retain the existing finiteness and bounded-above clauses. Extract F^a = top and F^(b+1) = bottom from the fixed-interval clause. Antitonicity and c <= a give top = F^a <= F^c, so F^c = top. Antitonicity and b+1 <= d+1 give F^(d+1) <= F^(b+1) = bottom, so F^(d+1) = bottom. Equality of the optional interval identifies all quantified endpoints with c,d. The remaining declarations are the explicit constructions recorded in the statement.
